deployed_via: commit-based release pipeline (deploy/build-release.sh + release-manager.php stage/build/contract-check/migrate-check/smoke-test-isolated/switch/rollback/smoke-test-live) — release id e01fcedaf660-2026-09-2107314
note: This is the last commit confirmed live in production as of this deploy. Update this file after every deploy made THROUGH this pipeline, so the next build's manifest.previous_commit is accurate.
release_contents: Admin Panel quality/performance audit fixes, in two commits deployed back-to-back: (1) 5fae07e — an 82-glyph icon subset (build-icon-subset.mjs) replacing the Zircos theme's full 5,936-glyph Tabler Icons set (was 801KB font + 242KB CSS on every admin page load; now 15.5KB + 3.5KB), plus 5 duplicate-looking sidebar label fixes found by the same audit (three section headers whose only child repeated the header's own word, two different modules both labelled 'আবেদনসমূহ'). (2) e01fced — packaging correction for an incident this same deploy caused (see incident_2026_09_20 below): moved the generated subset from public/brand-icons/ to public/brand/icons/, inside a directory the remote switch step's public-asset sync already copies recursively, instead of adding a new entry to that sync's hardcoded list.
incident_2026_09_20: 5fae07e switched live at 2026-09-20T20:31:02Z. The built artifact correctly contained public/brand-icons/{css,woff2} (asset contract verified this pre-deploy), but release-manager.php's `switch` step syncs public assets into the docroot via a HARDCODED list (build, brand, favicon.ico, robots.txt) baked into the remote tooling, not derived from the artifact contents — brand-icons/ was never in that list. The new layout referenced /brand-icons/provatferi-icons.css, which therefore 404'd on the live docroot: every .ti icon rendered at width 0 across the entire admin panel. Not caught immediately — verification checked /login, which uses a different layout (guest.blade.php) that never references the icon subset at all, and roughly 11 hours passed (session idle) before an authenticated /admin page was actually checked with a real browser and the failure was found. Rolled back at 2026-09-21T07:27:01Z (restored_from _previous-20260920-203101, failed release preserved at _rolled-back-20260921-072701 for the record). Root cause fixed in e01fced by relocating the subset to public/brand/icons/ — inside the 'brand' entry the remote sync already handles recursively — rather than touching release-manager.php's remote packaging list. Lesson recorded here so it isn't relearned: this pipeline's local build-release.sh packaging list and the REMOTE switch step's public-asset sync list are two separate lists that must be kept in sync by hand; a new top-level public/ directory needs BOTH updated, or nest it under one the remote side already syncs (brand/, build/) instead of adding a third list entry.
migrations_applied: None in either commit. migrate-check confirmed 'Nothing to migrate' before both the 5fae07e switch and the e01fced switch.
switch_note: Both switches clean (atomic_rename_ms 0.594 and 0.432 respectively, public_asset_sync_ms ~11-12ms, routes_changed false both times so route:cache correctly skipped). The e01fced switch was preceded by a rollback (see incident above), executed via release-manager.php rollback with no arguments, which restores CURRENT_RELEASE.json's previous_path.
smoke_test_live: Post-e01fced: ok:true. /login 200, /forgot-password 200, /admin 302 (unauthenticated redirect, expected). app_debug false. log_size_bytes_after_switch 0. THIS TIME additionally verified with an authenticated Puppeteer session hitting /admin directly (not /login) and screenshotting the rendered page — the check that should have run after 5fae07e's switch and didn't.
production_qa_evidence: Icon subset verified end-to-end post-fix: pre-switch cache-busted fetch of the new path confirmed 404 (ground truth), post-switch fetch confirmed 200 with byte-for-byte matching sizes (3554B CSS, 15868B woff2), and a full authenticated browser screenshot of /admin showed real rendered glyphs (sitemap/calendar/document/users icons on the dashboard cards) with zero failed network requests. A parallel full 19-page performance + duplicate-UI re-audit (same page set as the pre-fix baseline) came back 19/19 status 200, zero duplicate-UI findings, zero console errors, zero failed requests, icon sheet confirmed as /brand/icons/provatferi-icons.css with font-family tabler-icons on every page. QA cleanup: 3 disposable regression-diagnosis applications (VOL-2026-0001/0007/0008) and 3 disposable temp-admin accounts created across this session's audit passes were all purged (JobApplication hard-deletes; User soft-deletes so forceDelete was used) — explicitly leaving untouched one real application (VOL-2026-0009, westernwatch.bd@gmail.com) and one pre-existing unrelated temp-QA user (id 4, predates this session) that this process did not create.
performance_before_after: 19-page average, cold cache (cache disabled), real production, before 5fae07e vs after e01fced: load time 1129ms -> 715ms (-36.7%), total transferred 2729KB -> 1662KB (-39.1%, matching the 38.1% projected from local font/CSS size deltas), request count unchanged (20 avg both). TTFB rose 251ms -> 356ms and DCL rose 612ms -> 695ms between the two measurements; NOT attributed to this change (no backend/PHP code touched either commit) and treated as environmental/measurement noise between two single-pass runs at different times of day, noted here rather than silently omitted.
cron_timing_note: Cron runs in UTC; server Date header matched local UTC clock exactly both deploys. One-shot crons scheduled 5-6 minutes ahead on specific minutes, read once, then deleted immediately — cron slate confirmed empty before arming each next step, including immediately after the rollback (a completed one-shot cron entry was still listed until explicitly deleted, even though it had already fired — always delete a completed entry before checking the slate is 'empty', don't assume Hostinger auto-removes fired one-shots).
switch_gate_note: release-manager.php `switch` requires stage/build/contract_check/smoke_test_isolated but NOT migrate_apply, even when migrate-check reported pending migrations. Always read migrate-check yourself and run migrate-apply before scheduling switch. Neither release this round carried migrations, but the gate was still read both times.
asset_packaging_note: SEE incident_2026_09_20 above — this is now the authoritative note on the two-list packaging trap. Going forward: any new public/ top-level directory must either (a) be added to BOTH build-release.sh's tar list AND release-manager.php's remote switch-step sync list, with an explicit note in both files pointing at the other, or (b) be nested inside an existing synced directory (brand/, build/) to avoid the second list entirely — preferred, as done here.
upload_url_note: Generated via hosting_generateUploadURLV1 for provatferi.org (domain arg) fresh for each of: the two ERP release uploads this round, and three small self-deleting one-shot PHP scripts (temp-admin setup x2, final QA-data purge) staged briefly under public_html/admin/ — each confirmed 404 immediately after its single cron invocation. One of these scripts was accidentally executed early by a stray curl HEAD-style check against its own URL (fetching a script under a web-servable docroot runs it) — its effect (creating a temp admin) was idempotent/harmless and the same script's built-in purge step later found and removed the orphan by its naming pattern; lesson: never curl/fetch a staged one-shot script's URL to 'check if it's there' — that request executes it. Use the cron's own output or a HEAD-avoiding existence check instead.
